capabilities: Open the vault as a VS Code workspace from the ribbon, command palette or file-explorer context menu
Launch VS Code via the vscode:// URL scheme with a configurable protocol
Open the current file and jump to a specific line and character
Template the shell command with vault, file, folder, line and character variables
Point the URL method at VS Code variants such as Insiders or VSCodium
extras: The command template can execute arbitrary shell commands, so the README warns users to take caution; macOS, Flatpak and other setups need extra steps to make the code command available. Credits several contributors and links to sponsorship pages (GitHub, Ko-fi, PayPal).
motivation: Not stated beyond being a small utility; the README notes its function overlaps with other plugins but that it will be maintained anyway.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in way to hand the current vault or file over to VS Code for external editing, git work or linting.

relations.evidence: The context menu entry also appears in Notebook Navigator, on both files and folders
Thank you to the makers of the DEVONlink plugin, as it was a great starting point

summary: VS Code launcher that adds a ribbon button, file-explorer context menu entries and commands to open the vault as a Visual Studio Code workspace.
